questions.q: What is the main limitation of nodeSelector compared to node affinity?
options: nodeSelector cannot be used with any Pod spec
nodeSelector only supports exact label matches with no soft preference or richer expressions, while node affinity supports both required (hard) and preferred (soft) rules
nodeSelector works only on taints, not labels
nodeSelector is deprecated and produces an error if used
questions.explain: nodeSelector requires an exact match on every listed label with no notion of 'preferred but not required.' Node affinity offers the same hard-match behavior (required) plus a soft preference option, and richer matchExpressions.

questions.q: What does a taint on a node actually do?
options: It attracts Pods with matching labels toward that node
It repels Pods from the node unless they carry a matching toleration
It sets the node's resource requests automatically
It permanently removes the node from the cluster
questions.explain: A taint applied to a node rejects Pods that don't have a matching toleration — the opposite direction of affinity, which pulls Pods toward nodes.

questions.q: A node has a taint with effect NoExecute. What happens to a Pod already running on that node that does NOT tolerate the taint?
options: Nothing — NoExecute only affects Pods not yet scheduled
The Pod is evicted from the node, not just blocked from being newly scheduled there
The Pod is automatically given a matching toleration
The taint is ignored for already-running Pods under all effects
questions.explain: NoExecute is the most aggressive taint effect — it evicts Pods already running on the node that don't tolerate the taint, unlike NoSchedule, which only blocks new placements.

questions.q: Northbridge wants checkout's replicas spread across different nodes so a single node failure doesn't take down the whole service. Which mechanism achieves this?
options: Node affinity targeting a specific node label
A taint applied to the checkout Deployment
Pod anti-affinity using topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname with a labelSelector matching app: checkout
Setting minReplicas on a HorizontalPodAutoscaler
questions.explain: Pod anti-affinity with topologyKey set to the hostname label tells the scheduler not to place a Pod on a node that already has another Pod matching the given label selector — spreading replicas across nodes.

options: The affinity rule is only checked at scheduling time; a later label change on a running node does not cause already-placed Pods to be evicted
The rule is ignored entirely and has no effect
The Pod will be evicted immediately if the node's labels ever change
It means the rule only applies during the Pod's termination
questions.explain: IgnoredDuringExecution means the affinity/anti-affinity rule is evaluated only at scheduling time — if the node's labels change afterward, Pods already running there are not retroactively evicted.
